{{Short description|Dutch chemist and educator}}
[[File:ReneJanssen2015.jpg|thumb|René Janssen (2015)]]
'''René A.J. Janssen''' (born 1959 in Roermond, Netherlands) is a Dutch chemist who is Professor of the Moleculair Materials and Nanosystems group (M2N group) within the department of Chemical engineering and Chemistry at [[Eindhoven University of Technology]].

In 2013 Janssen won a 2.5 million euro grant by the [[European Research Council]] to develop methods to produce solar energy systems at a lower cost.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.ed.nl/regio/eindhoven/vijf-miljoen-subsidie-voor-hoogleraren-tu-e-1.3930450 |title=Vijf miljoen subsidie voor hoogleraren TU/e |language=Dutch |publisher=Eindhovens Dagblad |date=25 July 2013 |accessdate=12 June 2015}}</ref>

In 2015 he was one of four winners of the Dutch [[Spinoza Prize]].<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.nwo.nl/actueel/nieuws/2015/nwo-spinozapremies-voor-rene-janssen-birgit-meyer-aad-van-der-vaart-en-cisca-wijmenga.html |title=NWO-Spinozapremies voor René Janssen, Birgit Meyer, Aad van der Vaart en Cisca Wijmenga |language=Dutch |publisher=[[Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research]] |date=12 June 2015 |accessdate=12 June 2015}}</ref> Part of Janssen's research focuses on plastic solar cells and the storage of solar energy in solar cells.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.ed.nl/economie/spinozaprijs-voor-tu-e-hoogleraar-rene-janssen-1.4996774 |title=Spinozaprijs voor TU/e hoogleraar Rene Janssen |language=Dutch |publisher=Eindhovens |date=12 June 2015 |accessdate=12 June 2015}}</ref>

Since 2011 Janssen is member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/nl/leden/leden/11670 |title=René Janssen |language=Dutch |publisher=[[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] |date= |accessdate=12 June 2015}}</ref>
